metadata.case_name: WONG SUN CHEONG, SUING BY HIS NEXT FRIEND LEE YIN SHEUNG v. CHOI CHI KONG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: delivery man at Kai Ming Food Shop

injuries.source: P sustained severe head injuries as is borne out by the agreed medical evidence.

injuries.description: Fractures on the left side of his skull
injuries.source: Radiological investigations showed fractures on the left side of his skull, subarachnoid bleeding, subdural bleeding as well as contusion of the brain substance.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of skull or facial bones, part unspecified

P's brain injury was complicated by epileptic seizures in August 2012 but these had not recurred.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

manifestations.description: Prolonged post‑traumatic amnesia (estimated as over one month)
Dysphasia (problem with language; impaired ability to express himself; often using the wrong words; impairment of understanding verbal communications)
Cognitive dysfunction (naming difficulty; slowed comprehension of terms and instructions; MMSE 18/30 - mild to moderate dementia)
Epileptic seizures (status epilepticus in August 2012; on long term phenytoin)
Impaired balance / truncal ataxia (cannot walk heel to toe; walked stably but showing truncal ataxia)
Right leg mild spasticity with heightened reflexes
Unable to manage his own legal and financial affairs; not fully independent even inside the home
Not employable in any capacity (permanent loss of earning capacity 100%)

treatments_received: Emergency operation to evacuate blood clots and insert a ventricular drain (on day of injury)
Further emergency operation the following day to evacuate more blood clots
Cranioplasty in May 2012 to repair the skull defect with a metallic prosthesis
Admission to intensive care unit and intubation (August 2012)
Rehabilitation (transfer from QEH to Kowloon Hospital for rehabilitation)

losses.description: P is not employable in any capacity; his permanent loss of earning capacity was 100%.
P is not capable of managing his own legal and financial affairs and is not fully independent even inside the home.
Dysphasia with impaired ability to express himself and impaired understanding of verbal communications.
Cognitive dysfunction including naming difficulty, slowed comprehension and MMSE 18/30 (mild to moderate dementia).
Impaired balance and truncal ataxia; cannot walk heel to toe; required supervision when walking.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Incontinence and impaired balance requiring ongoing care and assistance (including diapers and a carer).
